thread.title: India, China Reach Eight-Point Border Consensus, Add New Military Meeting Points To Strengthen LAC Management

title: India, China Reach Eight-Point Border Consensus, Add New Military Meeting Points To Strengthen LAC Management
text:
Politics
Swarajya Staff
Aug 27, 2026 | Updated 09:03 AM GMT+5:30

India and China have reached an eight-point consensus following high-level boundary talks in Beijing, with both nations committing to promptly address border situations through existing diplomatic and military channels.
National Security Adviser Ajit Doval and Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi co-chaired the 25th round of special representatives' talks on 25 August, marking continued engagement on the long-standing boundary dispute.
The two sides agreed that any situation between their armies in border areas would be addressed promptly to resolve outstanding issues and avoid misunderstanding along the Line of Actual Control.
Two additional meeting points were established for holding the General Level Mechanism and Senior Highest Military Commander meetings, strengthening the framework for on-ground communication between military forces.
Both nations decided that the Expert Group on Boundary Delimitation and Working Group on Border Management would advance discussions on boundary delimitation and border management.
The first task for both groups will be to agree on their respective terms of reference, setting the stage for substantive negotiations on the disputed 3,488-kilometre Himalayan boundary.
India and China discussed ways to improve understanding of the LAC in appropriate areas for better border management and to maintain peace and tranquillity in border areas.
The discussions also aimed to create an atmosphere for healthy development of bilateral relations, which have been strained since the 2020 Galwan Valley clash that resulted in casualties on both sides.
The 25th round of talks concluded with an agreement to hold the 26th round of special representatives' talks in India in 2027, signalling continued engagement on the boundary issue.
The discussions come amid broader efforts by both Asian powers to stabilise relations and manage differences through dialogue, though a final settlement of the boundary question remains unresolved.
